topics.topic: Atomic ordering of last-request updates against session expiry
questions: Since every ordinary owner request changes last_request, must reads and refused requests take the session lock, contrary to the statement that other requests are not held by state-changing requests, or is last_request updated outside that lock?

How is every valid request's arrival atomically ordered against the expiry pass, especially when a request arrives before the idle deadline but its last-request update races with a pass after the deadline?
How is last_request updated atomically with the expiry pass, especially for a request that must take the import lock before its session lock?

judgement.why: The same question about atomically ordering request arrival, idle renewal and expiry was already answered on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Atomic ordering of session validity, last-request refresh, and expiry
quotes:
An owner
   request is any request to the owner interface that
   carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30
   minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts; before the
   first request it runs from the sign-in.

Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).
precedent.why: Validity and idle renewal are explicitly decided at request arrival, so a request arriving before the limit remains admitted even if a sweep later obtains the lock.

topics.topic: Authentication of readable backup metadata and key-digest construction
questions: Must the readable record be cryptographically authenticated and bound to the encrypted store, and which digest algorithm and representation identify the key?
What digest algorithm and representation are used, and is this readable record authenticated so Registry can detect alteration before trusting it for scheduling, display and deletion?
Is this unencrypted record cryptographically authenticated and bound to the encrypted store, and which fields are checked against the decrypted contents?
Which digest or key identifier is stored, whether it is salted or keyed, and whether it is computed from the configured text, decoded bytes or derived encryption key?

judgement.why: The same question about authenticating readable backup metadata and constructing the key digest was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Backup encryption format, key fingerprint construction, and authentication of readable metadata
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Backup authenticated-encryption construction and file format
questions: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, key derivation and ciphertext format are required, and how is a key longer than the algorithm's key size handled?
Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, key derivation or normalization, file framing and authenticated data are required?
Which encryption algorithm, mode, nonce generation, key derivation and authentication rules make a backup encrypted and valid?

judgement.why: The same question about the authenticated-encryption construction and backup container format was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Backup encryption, key digest, authentication, and container format
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Configuration value validation, secret byte encoding, and backup-key representation
questions: How are environment-variable text values converted to bytes for length, equality, credential comparison and use as the backup key, and is the backup key raw text, hex, base64 or another encoding?
What makes each credential, token, backup key and path well formed, and in which encoding are environment-string secret lengths and equality measured as bytes?

How are environment strings converted to bytes for length, equality, authentication and backup encryption, and may the backup key have any length above 32 bytes or must it be decoded or derived into a fixed-size cryptographic key?

judgement.why: The same question about secret encoding, byte length, equality and conversion into a backup key was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Byte encoding, length measurement, equality, and comparison of secrets
quotes:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.

A presented secret is compared in constant time; no secret enters a record,
   a log line, an audit entry, a diagnostic or an answer (R0-23, R0-37).
precedent.why: The textual or binary representation, decoding, equality and byte-counting rules for credential fields are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Configuration variable names and overall schema
questions: What are the exact recognized variable names and the well-formedness rules for each value, without which Registry cannot identify an unknown item or perform the ordered checks?
What is the exact environment-variable name for each required item and each of the four service tokens?
What are the exact environment-variable names and the syntax and validity rules for the store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential and four service tokens?

quotes:
The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says; no other variable is read or
   checked. It holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 9).

A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start; Registry applies no
   default to any item.
judgement.why: Exact environment-field names and the encoded syntax and field-level validity rules of configuration values are State 6 contract details.

topics.topic: Expiry-pass initial timing and recurring cadence
questions: Does the first pass run immediately or after 60 seconds, is the cadence measured from process start or the previous pass, and what happens when a pass lasts longer than 60 seconds?
Does the first pass run at process start or 60 seconds later, and after a delayed pass are missed passes skipped or run to restore the original cadence?
Is the first pass made immediately or 60 seconds after start, and are later passes fixed to start-time boundaries or scheduled 60 seconds after the preceding pass finishes?

judgement.why: The same question about the cleanup pass's first run, cadence, delay and overlap was already judged behaviorally indifferent on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Cleanup-pass first-run, cadence, delay, overlap, and catch-up rules
quotes:
Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.

A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check.
precedent.why: The limits themselves determine request refusal exactly, so the first tick, delayed-tick policy and overlap handling affect only internal reclamation of already inaccessible session state.

topics.topic: Backup audit metadata when the audit history is empty
questions: What value is recorded and what check passes when a new store has never written an audit entry and its audit log is empty?
What value is recorded and checked when the snapshot has never written an audit entry?

judgement.why: The same question about representing and checking the audit sequence when the history is empty was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Backup audit-sequence metadata for empty or pruned audit histories
quotes:
It
   records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it,
   the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key it was
   made with (never the key); its age is counted from that instant.

Second, it
   writes the backup under a temporary name and checks it: it decrypts it
   into a second temporary file, opens that for reading only, checks that it
   is the store version of its release, that the store's own integrity check
   passes and that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number, and
   removes it; a backup that passes is renamed to its kept name, one that
   fails is deleted.
precedent.why: The empty-log representation of the sequence metadata and its encoded validation rule are field-type and backup-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Backup scheduled-date semantics under clock and date changes
questions: If the clock jumps from before 03:00 on one UTC date to after 03:00 on a later date, is a run made for the newly observed date despite there being no earlier observation of that same date?
If the UTC date changes between the scheduler's qualifying clock observation and the snapshot instant, which date is marked as run and used to decide whether another run may occur?

quotes:
a date's
   run starts at its first look at or after 03:00 of that date when an
   earlier look of the same process saw that date before 03:00, and no kept
   backup of that date exists

after a clock set forward it runs only for
   the date it then sees pass 03:00, and the dates jumped over get no run.
judgement.why: A forward jump into a later date after 03:00 both fails the required earlier observation of that same date and is said to run for the date then seen passing 03:00.

topics.topic: Expiry-pass session traversal and lock granularity
questions: How is the set of sessions traversed while sign-ins create sessions and sign-outs or earlier pass work remove them, and does the pass hold the import lock once for the whole traversal or reacquire it for each session?
Does one pass hold the import lock for the whole sweep, and does it hold all session locks together or acquire, decide and release them one at a time?

judgement.why: The same question about expiry-pass traversal membership and import-lock granularity was already judged behaviorally indifferent on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Expiry-pass import-lock scope and iteration membership
quotes:
Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.

A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check.
precedent.why: Holding the import lock for the whole visit or per session, and snapshotting or dynamically enumerating sessions, changes only internal waiting and reclamation because validity is decided from the fixed limits at request arrival.

topics.topic: Kept and temporary backup filename construction and collisions
questions: What exact instant precision and filename construction are used, how are temporary names made unique, and what happens if a non-regular file or an existing temporary file occupies the selected name?
What are the exact kept and temporary prefixes, the store temporary suffix, the instant serialization and the collision-free filename construction?

judgement.why: The same question about backup filename grammar, timestamp encoding, uniqueness and collisions was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Backup filename grammar, uniqueness, and existing-name collision handling
quotes:
Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release
   declares, neither beginning with the other;

A kept
   name is made from the backup's instant and is never overwritten: a backup
   whose kept name exists, or whose rename fails, is deleted and the run
   fails.
precedent.why: The prefixes, timestamp encoding and filename grammar are backup-format encodings owned by State 6; the texts already state that an existing kept name makes the new run fail without overwriting it.

topics.topic: Locking protocol for clearing uploads across sessions after import
questions: When an accepted import changes uploads belonging to other sessions, must it also take each other session's lock, and in what acquisition and release pattern?
Must an accepted import acquire every affected session lock before clearing that session's upload, and if so, in what session order and whether all session locks are held together or one at a time?

judgement.why: The same question about taking other session locks while an accepted import clears their uploads was already judged behaviorally indifferent on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Locking required when an accepted import drops uploads in other sessions
quotes:
Uploads
   and every other request that reads or changes an uploaded file — showing
   the mapping or the import's confirmation step, confirming, a sign-out —
   take the instance's one import lock first, then their session's lock
   (A13), check the closure while holding them, and hold both until done;

An uploaded file is changed only by a holder of the import lock: an
   accepted import, holding it, drops every session's upload; the upload of
   a session ended by its limits goes with the session, when Registry ends it
   (A13 rule 2).
precedent.why: The import lock already excludes every other operation that can read or change an upload, so additionally taking the other sessions' locks changes only internal waiting and not any specified result.

topics.topic: Startup behavior when a stale temporary store cannot be removed
questions: If the final store is absent and the stale temporary store cannot be removed, does startup fail or try to create/overwrite/reuse that temporary file?
What happens if the stale temporary store file cannot be removed: does startup fail, continue to inspect the configured store, or report and continue as it does for a stale backup temporary?

quotes:
A failed start leaves no
   file it made but a probe it could not remove, which the next start or run
   removes with the other temporary files; a stale temporary file a start
   cannot remove is reported and does not stop the start.

When the store's
   configured file does not exist and its directory does, Registry makes a new,
   empty store of the running release's version there at the start, under a
   temporary name — the store's name with a suffix the release declares —
   that it renames to the store's name only once the store is complete; at
   every start it first removes a file of that temporary name, left by an
   interrupted start, and no other file there;
judgement.divergence: One implementation fails startup when the final store is absent and the occupied temporary name cannot be removed; another continues by overwriting, reusing or choosing around that file, which the owner notices as different service availability and potentially different store contents.
judgement.why: The text says removal failure does not stop startup but does not define how creation under the still-occupied mandatory temporary name proceeds.

topics.topic: Startup cleanup policy for backup temporary files
questions: At what point does startup scan the backup location, exactly which temporary-prefix files does it remove, and does a failure to remove them merely report or fail the writable-location check?
Does every Registry start remove files under A18's temporary prefix, including an owner-only start, or are they removed only by a backup run?

quotes:
A failed start leaves no
   file it made but a probe it could not remove, which the next start or run
   removes with the other temporary files; a stale temporary file a start
   cannot remove is reported and does not stop the start.

First, it removes every file under the
   temporary prefix; if a removal fails, the run stops there.
judgement.divergence: One implementation removes every backup temporary-prefix file during every startup, including owner-only startup, while another leaves them until a backup run; the owner notices different retained files, diagnostics and disk consumption.
judgement.why: The startup text promises removal on the next start or run, while only the backup-run cleanup operation and its failure behavior are defined.

topics.topic: Store engine and exact integrity-check procedure
questions: Which store engine and exact integrity operation define this refusal condition, including what result is a pass?
What exact engine operation and result constitute the full integrity check, including whether foreign-key checks, schema checks and application-level invariants are included?

quotes:
otherwise
   the store must open for reading and writing, pass the store engine's full
   integrity check — the same as a backup's check (A18 rule 4) — and carry
   the store
   version of the running release, and a store of another version, or one
   that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version is
   a step of the release, not of the start.

Second, it
   writes the backup under a temporary name and checks it: it decrypts it
   into a second temporary file, opens that for reading only, checks that it
   is the store version of its release, that the store's own integrity check
   passes and that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number, and
   removes it; a backup that passes is renamed to its kept name, one that
   fails is deleted.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats only the store engine's basic physical-integrity result as sufficient, while another also checks foreign keys, schema consistency or application invariants; the owner notices corrupted stores or backups being accepted by one and refused by the other.
judgement.why: The refusal rule depends on a “full integrity check” whose required checks and passing result are not defined.

topics.topic: Validity of requests admitted before their session ends
questions: What prevents the expiry pass from ending and clearing a session after a request passed its session check but before that request acquired the required locks or used its pending confirmation or uploaded file?

If a request passes the session check before a limit but waits for a lock until the expiry pass or sign-out ends the session, must that request still complete, or must validity be checked again under the lock?

judgement.why: The same question about requests admitted before expiry or sign-out completing after the session ends was already answered on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Reservation and ordering of admitted requests against expiry, sign-out, and imports
quotes:
A sign-out is applied in turn with the session's other requests that
   change it: one admitted before it completes its change to the store, and
   leaves nothing in the ended session.
precedent.why: A request admitted before sign-out completes its store change even if it acquires the session lock later, while no state remains in the ended session.

topics.topic: Clock used for session limits and cleanup cadence
questions: Which clock governs session limits and the cleanup cadence, and what happens when the system wall clock moves backward or forward?

topics.topic: Fate of other sessions' pending import confirmations after acceptance
questions: Does acceptance also clear pending import confirmations in other sessions, or do those values remain pending until submitted, replaced, expired or their sessions end?

topics.topic: Portion of a backup readable without the encryption key
questions: What exactly may be read without the key: only the stated metadata record, or no part of the backup file?

topics.topic: Snapshot of sessions affected by an accepted import
questions: At what instant is “every owner session” determined when sign-ins and sign-outs can occur concurrently with the accepted import?

topics.topic: Store and backup location parsing and resolution
questions: Are relative locations allowed, and if so relative to what stable directory; what exact path forms and target types count as well formed before resolution?

topics.topic: Synchronization and failure semantics of backup-status reads
questions: How is the status read synchronized with rename and deletion, and what answer is required if the selected file disappears or becomes unreadable during the read?
